results.evidence: Retry searches (extended web search, MP forum, SummitPost north face, LA Mountaineers NAC pages, Gripped) found only the regular North Face and a forum mention of an ice runnel out left, no pitch count for this variation. The row itself says one true pitch plus an easier second rope length, so 1 is not provably wrong.

Route listing: 909 m, lower half soloed or simul-climbed to a 50 m ice curtain, then 3 more ice pitches, so well over one pitch. A 2010 climber blog says up to 6 ice pitches (about 3 by rope length) on top of the long lower section; Gripped gives about 1,000 m. Sources disagree on the exact count, so the false 1 is blanked.

Route listing gives 3,600 ft (1,091 m) and 6 to 10 roped pitches on the buttress plus about 6 more on the upper East Ridge; the AAJ report describes roughly six roped pitches on the lower buttress alone. Both prove it is far more than 1 pitch but no total is stated, so the false 1 is blanked.

Mountain Project lists 7 pitches (about 800 ft) and a guide-service program page independently describes three pitches on the first tower, three on the second and a seventh reaching the ridge. The overview's 5 pitches is a towers-only count with a 70 m rope, an alternative way of splitting the same ground, so the row value 7 stands.

Retry: MP gives 5.9 overall, 4 pitches, with one user's P3 at 5.10b; the AAC note calls it a moderate classic, and a MP forum thread mentions some tricky/aid climbing. No guidebook, thecrag or SummitPost page states pitch grades, so neither number can be overturned by two sources.

The route's own pitch lengths (25, 45, 63 m, plus an optional 10 m) total roughly 133-143 m and the party's write-up gives 150-160 m, both well below the stored 366 m (the 1,200 ft header figure). Two accounts contradict 366 but give slightly different lengths, so length_m is blanked. A further search for other pages on this 2023 route found none.

The AAJ report and the climber's blog both describe a three-day, 2,800 ft climb with an aid headwall, a M5-6 chimney, a dihedral, several WI3-4 pitches, a WI/AI6 drip and a final WI3 pitch, clearly many pitches. No total is given, so the false 1 is blanked.

Retry searches show only the route's own Mountain Project page (5.10b/c PG13, 6 pitches, pitch 1 5.10a) and its stats page; the Nesakwatch guide pages and trip reports cover other lines. The crux may be unlisted, so the header cannot be overturned.

results.evidence: Retry: ClubTread thread, both MP directions and Ocean to Alpine confirm a rappel into the notch after the au cheval but no source names the compass end; the two MP pages themselves conflict.
Retry searches (extended, thecrag, AAJ, OpenBeta) found only the Mountain Project page, which says 7 in the header and nine in the text; no independent page gives a pitch count for this line.
